properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the
increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides
will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily
high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach
7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records
set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides
will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably
higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in
exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with
sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 3.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Tuesday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

or waterspouts. Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and
blow around unsecured objects.

properties.description:

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has allowed the St Johns River at Sanford to continue
rising through Minor Flood Stage. River levels are forecast to climb
through Moderate Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
anticipated thereafter, reaching Major Flood Stage by the middle of
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 7.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:30 PM EST Saturday was 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 8.1 feet Wednesday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. The river level will continue
a slow rise through tonight and is expected to become steady this
weekend into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This will set an all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 PM EST Friday was 18.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
break points.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM
Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has allowed the St Johns River at Sanford to continue
rising through Moderate Flood Stage, Additional rises are anticipated
through next week, reaching Major Flood Stage by the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 7.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue a steady rise,
reaching 8.2 feet late next week. Additional rises are possible
thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

week.

forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration

properties.description:
AVWREV

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002
(Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large
avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49)
on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the
greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas,
not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs
exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating
dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is
overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas.
Avalanches could run down into treed terrain.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche
conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below
backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH
avalanche danger.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org
for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage
area of this or any avalanche center.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the
increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides
will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily
high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach
7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain
around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell
Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf
beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above
baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent
observations.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.1 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 3.0 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday,
2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft
above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above
normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above
normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions
include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.

Areas of fog will continue to develop across parts of southeast
Georgia and northeast Florida through the early morning hours.
Patchy dense fog is expected which reduces visibilities to less
than 1/2 mile on roadways. Fog should then dissipate by mid
morning, by around 10 AM. It is possible fog could become dense
over more locations which would require a dense fog advisory

over short distances. If driving this morning, slow down, use
low-beam headlights and leave extra distance between you and the
vehicle in front of you.

properties.description:
Areas of fog will continue to develop across parts of southeast
Georgia and northeast Florida through the early morning hours.
Patchy dense fog is expected which reduces visibilities to less
than 1/2 mile on roadways. Fog should then dissipate by mid
morning, by around 10 AM. It is possible fog could become dense
over more locations which would require a dense fog advisory.

The nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly
over short distances. If driving this morning, slow down, use
low-beam headlights and leave extra distance between you and the
vehicle in front of you.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage and has
now quickly passed record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall over
the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above record
flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding

Washington Coast.

AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday
night through late Thursday night.

during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well

overflow flooding is expected. Coastal residents in the warned
area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate
action to protect life and property.

flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 AM EST Friday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Tuesday
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through next week. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage late this weekend, with additional rises
thereafter.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 5.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet Wednesday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to
11 feet building to 15 to 20 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tides between about 800 AM
and 1000 AM.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM
PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday
to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory
will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning
before Wednesday. Additional products will likely be needed
into Friday.

properties.instruction:

for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW)
at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25
AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.instruction:

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

dangerous surf conditions.

shore and call or wave for help.

sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,

currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

Thursday with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf
Advisory will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf
Warning before Wednesday. Additional products will likely be
needed into Friday.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at
8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM
Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday,
2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4
ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These
predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf
heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10
feet on west-facing beaches.

predictions based on trends in recent observations.

ground level.

Coast zones.

expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast
and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional
products will likely be needed into Friday.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage this weekend due to
heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination with
strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Friday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.1 feet by Sunday.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to

Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
